name: message
title: Message
purpose: One row of an agent transcript: a prompt, the agent's text, a tool call, its result, a denial, usage or the end of a turn.
whenToUse: For each event of an agent's turn, as a list item in the transcript's ol or ul, oldest first.
To show what a tool was asked to do and what it returned, in mono, at phone width.
whenNotToUse: For a request that still waits for the reader's answer. Use an approval, which carries Allow and Decline.
For the note that the agent is still working. Use streaming as the last row.
For a message about the app itself, such as a lost connection. Use an alert or a banner.

variants.name: agent
variants.use: The default, with no modifier class. Text the agent wrote. Label it with the agent's name.

variants.name: user
variants.use: A prompt the reader sent. Label it You.

variants.name: tool-call
variants.use: A tool the agent ran: the tool name, then the command or path. Put long arguments in a details element whose summary keeps the label, the tool name and a short command.

variants.name: tool-result
variants.use: What a tool returned. Show the first lines, and put the rest in a details element whose summary reads Show full output.

variants.name: denied
variants.use: A call that was refused. Say what was not run and why.

variants.name: usage
variants.use: A quiet line of figures for the turn, such as tokens and duration.

variants.name: turn-end
variants.use: A quiet closing row under a rule, saying that the turn finished and how: completed, stopped or ended with an error.

accessibility: Each row is an li in an ol or ul. Put role="log" and an accessible name on the list when rows are added while the reader watches, so new rows are announced.

Every row starts with gw-message__label, which says the kind in words: You, Claude Code, Tool call, Tool result, Denied, Usage, End. The kind is never the colour alone, and the denied row's icon is drawn by the stylesheet.
Write transcript text as text, never as markup, and write out characters that cannot be seen.

Collapsed arguments and long output use a native details element, with no script. Its summary holds text that says what is inside. Enter and Space open and close it, and its pointer target is 44px tall.
When output is cut short, the lines after the preview go in the details element, so opened text continues where the preview stopped.
The app sets nothing but the open attribute, which the browser manages.
